basis: Human-authored review objectives after inspecting extracted text and original PDF figures. These are acceptance criteria, not a measured model score or a complete scientific answer key.

objectives: Explain risk pooling and why combining sufficiently independent risks can reduce relative uncertainty.
Explain the role and assumptions of the law of large numbers in insurance pricing.
Distinguish a contractual premium from the uncertain claims illustrated on the slide.
requiredContext: Dependence and correlated losses limit diversification.
Use an explicitly hypothetical numerical example only if its assumptions and inputs are stated.
mustNotInvent: The law of large numbers guarantees a profitable insurer or perfectly predicts every claim.

objectives: Distinguish product families by the need served, insured risk and financial feature.
Explain how reinsurance protects an insurer and how a captive finances a group's own risks.
Apply the classification to a clear hypothetical customer need without treating overlapping labels as exclusive.
requiredContext: Explain duration and investment sensitivity in life products, and frequency/severity in property and casualty.
Course product labels can overlap; purpose and risk transfer matter.
mustNotInvent: Every product belongs to one universally exclusive legal category.
A jurisdiction-specific product rule that is neither documented nor identified as uncertain.

objectives: Identify that the chart compares premium income of European insurance groups in 2022, in USD billions.
Distinguish premium income from profit and from a percentage market share.
Explain why comparisons require compatible year, scope and metric rather than memorising a long ranking.
requiredContext: The figure visibly ranks AXA, Allianz and Generali first in this particular chart.
Added explanations about premiums must be identified as background, not falsely attributed to the chart.
mustNotInvent: These are percentages of a defined European market.
A company with more premium income necessarily has more profit or better performance.

objectives: Read the chart as life-insurer market shares based on gross premiums written in 2025.
Explain the numerator and denominator needed for a market-share percentage.
If an application is offered, state its inputs explicitly: 41.8% plus 11.8% equals 53.6% for the two indicated slices.
requiredContext: The figure shows Swiss Life at 41.8% and Helvetia at 11.8%.
Any geographic scope inferred from neighbouring slides must remain distinct from what the figure explicitly states.
mustNotInvent: Market share proves causation, superior service or profitability.
A hypothetical percentage computation is a new real-world finding.
The historical figure establishes today's market shares.

objectives: Explain the roles of actuarial, risk management, finance, investment management, compliance and internal audit in an insurance company.
Distinguish risk management, compliance and internal audit by their objectives.
Explain a concrete hypothetical collaboration between functions without inventing reporting lines absent from the slide.
requiredContext: The slide describes a possible structure, not a universal organizational requirement.
Added professional context should clarify responsibilities and coordination.
mustNotInvent: Every insurer uses the depicted structure or reporting lines.
A particular jurisdiction's mandatory governance arrangements without an adequate source.
